FXUS63 KIWX 280626
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
226 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Warm and dry today with highs in the mid 70s.

- Very light rain is possible on Thursday followed by slightly
  cooler temperatures.

- More rain is possible over the weekend with the best chances
  on Sunday but forecast confidence for this period remains low.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 226 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Another warm and tranquil day as ridge rebuilds behind departing
shortwave responsible for current mid/high clouds and virga. 
These clouds will scatter during the day and highs climb into 
the mid 70s for most given some light SW flow/WAA. Mild 
overnight lows expected given increasing SW gradient and clouds 
ahead of the next cold front. Only mid 50s expected in our NW 
zones. As previously mentioned, this cold front will feature a 
moderate prefrontal theta-e surge (thanks to a 30-40 kt LLJ) 
capable of finally moistening very dry/stable airmass that has 
been in place for quite some time. However, better mid and upper
level dynamics remain displaced well to our north. Decent 
1000-850mb convergence within a moderate theta-e ridge will be 
enough to spark a narrow line of light showers on Thu but total 
rain amounts will be very light (a few hundredths at best). The 
best chances will be in our northwest where better moisture and 
forcing reside. Areas south of US-24 likely remain dry. No 
thunderstorms expected given virtually no instability so overall
no impacts anticipated. Postfrontal airmass is cooler but not 
particularly cold given it is almost Halloween. Lows Thu night 
dip near 40F with highs on Fri in the 60s (still above normal).

Forecast details for the weekend and early next week remain 
uncertain. A subtropical Pacific jet streak/shortwave lifts into
the region in piecemeal fashion over the weekend followed by 
the eastward ejection (in some fashion) of a Pacific Northwest 
upper low. This is a convoluted mid/upper level pattern 
evolution that models are still struggling with immensely. The 
initial shortwave and theta-e surge could bring some light rain 
to our W/NW counties early Sat but CVA and moisture advection 
are both very meager. Any rain will be light and it could easily
remain entirely dry. These low chance PoP's extend into the 
early evening. Some light sprinkles can't be entirely ruled out 
for Sat evening activities but overall impacts should be 
minimal. Better rain chances arrive on Sun but even this is no 
slam dunk. Several guidance sources suggest the main trough and 
better moisture pass just to our S/SE. Attention then turns to 
large upper low migrating across the country. Models continue to
show an incredibly high degree of spread with how this upper 
low evolves. Expect we will get some more widespread/moderate 
rain out of it at some point but timing is very up in the air.

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z THURSDAY/...
Issued at 130 AM EDT Wed Oct 28 2026

Midlevel shortwave supporting widespread 12 kft ceilings this
morning but low levels remain very dry and VFR conditions will
persist. Latest guidance shows a much lower chance for fog
development. High clouds briefly scatter later today but return
early Thursday morning as a weak cold front approaches the
region. No aviation impact anticipated.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...None.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...None.

&&

$$

spc.text:
SPC AC 280526

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1226 AM CDT Wed Oct 28 2026

   Valid 281200Z - 291200Z

   ...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTIONS OF
   EAST-CENTRAL MINNESOTA AND WEST-CENTRAL WISCONSIN....

   ...SUMMARY...
   A few severe thunderstorms are possible over the Upper Mississippi
   Valley on Wednesday with some tornado potential. Isolated large hail
   and damaging winds will also be possible.

   ...Synopsis...
   The overall mid-level pattern across the CONUS will become more
   zonal through the day today. Within this more zonal pattern, a
   mid-level shortwave trough will traverse the northern Plains. A weak
   surface low, associated with this mid-level trough, will deepen as
   it moves northeastward through the day. Elsewhere, high pressure
   will dominate through the day and evening. 

   ...Upper Mississippi Valley...
   Low-level moisture will advect northward today as a surface low,
   currently analyzed across southeast Colorado, deepens and moves
   northeastward to the Upper Midwest. This will result in weak
   instability into southern and central Minnesota with dewpoints in
   the upper 50s. During peak heating, storms are expected to develop
   near this surface low within the weakly unstable zone. Veered wind
   profiles and strong deep-layer shear will support a discrete mode
   including the potential for supercells. In fact, wind profiles are
   quite favorable within this zone with instability being the primary
   limiting factor. However, it would only take an increase of a few
   degrees in the dewpoint and/or temperature for greater instability
   and potentially a more impactful event. Therefore, while the
   forecast remains conditional, the ceiling could involve strong
   tornado potential. Therefore, added a Slight Risk, driven by tornado
   probabilities, for a small portion of eastern Minnesota and western
   Wisconsin in the vicinity of the surface low near peak heating where
   a several hour window of severe weather potential may exist. Shear
   and storm mode will support some hail potential, but the overall
   weaker instability precludes higher probabilities. The greatest
   damaging wind potential will likely be along the warm front ahead of
   the surface low where the potential for upscale growth is the
   greatest. However, even within this zone, the wind threat should
   remain somewhat subdued given the weak instability along this zone.

   ..Bentley/Halbert-E.. 10/28/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 280518

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1218 AM CDT Wed Oct 28 2026

   Valid 291200Z - 301200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorms are not expected on Thursday.

   ...Southern Rockies to Southern Plains vicinity...

   Upper ridging will begin the period over the southern/central Plains
   to the Mid/Lower MS Valley vicinity. The ridge will weaken across
   the southern Plains as a shortwave impulse ejects from northern
   Mexico into TX/NM. Meanwhile, another shortwave upper trough will
   move east across the Great Lakes vicinity. At the surface, a cold
   front will extend from the upper Great Lakes to central KS Thursday
   morning. The northern extent of the front will continue to develop
   east/southeast across portions of the Midwest, while the western
   extent of the front advances northward across the central Plains
   within the low-level warm advection regime beneath the upper ridge.

   Southerly low-level flow will transport modest boundary layer
   moisture northward across TX/OK/KS and the Lower MO Valley. This
   will support generally modest destabilization in the 500-1000 J/kg
   MLCAPE range, though a few areas across OK/KS may see values
   approaching 1500 J/kg. Showers and thunderstorms are expected to
   develop within the broad warm advection regime, aided by modest
   large-scale ascent from the ejecting weak midlevel trough, from
   NM/TX into OK/KS from midday into the evening. Vertical shear is
   forecast to remain weak, limiting organized strong/severe
   thunderstorm potential despite modest instability.

   ..Leitman.. 10/28/2026

spc.text:
SPC AC 280644

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0144 AM CDT Wed Oct 28 2026

   Valid 301200Z - 311200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe thunderstorm potential appears low on Friday.

   ...Synopsis...

   Showers and thunderstorms will again be possible on Friday across
   portions of the south-central U.S. as a weak midlevel shortwave
   trough continues to slowly lift northeast across the
   southern/central Plains. Weak instability and limited vertical shear
   will preclude severe thunderstorm potential. 

   Further west, southerly low-level flow will maintain 50s to near 60
   F surface dewpoints across southern AZ as a weak upper shortwave
   trough moves across the Lower CO Valley and Southwest. Cool
   temperatures aloft will support steep midlevel lapse rates atop the
   relatively moist boundary layer, fostering areas of modest
   destabilization. Isolated to scattered thunderstorm development will
   be possible, though deep-layer shear is expected to remain somewhat
   weak (15-25 kt effective shear). Currently, severe thunderstorm
   potential appears limited, but a stronger storm or two could produce
   small hail. Trends bear watching as any uptick in instability or
   strengthening shear could support a more isolated risk for severe
   thunderstorms across southern/central AZ.

   ..Leitman.. 10/28/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
